claims.quote: I do not think that it is asking too much of the reader's faith in progress to assume that so far as a light powerful engine goes, comparatively noiseless, smooth-running, not obnoxious to sensitive nostrils, and altogether suitable for high road traffic, the problem will very speedily be solved.
claims.description: Predicts that light, powerful, quiet, clean motor engines suited to road vehicles will soon be perfected.

claims.quote: sooner or later, no doubt, the numerous advantages of such an arrangement will lead to the organization of large carrier companies, using such motor trucks to carry goods in bulk or parcels on the high roads.
claims.description: Predicts large road-haulage companies using motor trucks to carry bulk goods and parcels.

claims.quote: It will be capable of a day's journey of three hundred miles or more, long before the developments to be presently foreshadowed arrive.
claims.description: Predicts hired or privately owned motor carriages able to travel 300+ miles in a day, replacing first-class rail travel for most journeys.

claims.quote: And thirdly there will be the motor omnibus, attacking or developing out of the horse omnibus companies and the suburban lines.
claims.description: Predicts motor omnibuses replacing horse omnibuses and competing with suburban railways.

claims.quote: they will attempt to secure, and, it may be, after tough legislative struggles, will secure the power to form private roads of a new sort, upon which their vehicles will be free to travel up to the limit of their very highest possible speed.
claims.description: Predicts dedicated high-speed private roads for motor traffic, segregated from horses and pedestrians (precursor of motorways).
claims.stated_time: probably even in the present decade

claims.quote: there are now so many thousand miles of these roads already established in America and Germany and elsewhere.
claims.description: Predicts that by 1910 thousands of miles of special motor roads will exist in America and Germany.

claims.quote: Their traffic in opposite directions will probably be strictly separated, and it will no doubt habitually disregard complicated and fussy regulations
claims.description: Predicts motor roads with separated opposite-direction lanes and grade-separated junctions using bridges rather than level crossings.

claims.quote: some at least of the railway companies will hasten to replace their flanged rolling stock by carriages with rubber tyres, remove their rails, broaden their cuttings and embankments, raise their bridges, and take to the new ways of traffic.
claims.description: Suggests some railway companies may convert their rights-of-way into rubber-tyred motor roads.

claims.quote: if one could write smoothly and easily at a steady table, read papers, have one's hair cut, and dine in comfort
claims.description: Imagines long-distance trains redesigned with steady tables, barbers and dining so travel is comfortable even if slower.

claims.quote: Almost all will probably be still in existence and in divers ways busy, spite of the swarming new highways I have ventured to foreshadow, a hundred years from now.
claims.description: Predicts railways will survive a century hence in specialized roles (bulk goods, cheap excursions) rather than disappear.

claims.quote: step by step with these developments will come a very considerable acceleration of the ferry traffic of the narrow seas through such improvements as the introduction of turbine engines.
claims.description: Predicts faster cross-channel ferry services using turbine engines.

claims.quote: the centripetal pressure of the congested towns of our epoch may ultimately be very greatly relieved
claims.description: Predicts that congestion in the dense great cities will eventually be relieved as population disperses outward.

claims.quote: These things may be the first beginning of a process of restriction that may go far.
claims.description: Predicts increasing regulation and restriction of vehicular traffic in city streets, returning towns toward pedestrian use.

claims.quote: there is one conceivable means of transit that is not simply frequent but continuous, that may be joined or left at any point without a stoppage, that could be adapted to many existing streets at the level or quite easily sunken in tunnels, or elevated above the street level
claims.description: Proposes continuous moving platforms (moving walkways) as urban mass transit, sunken, at-grade or elevated.

claims.quote: we should have the upper platform running round the circle at a pace of twenty-eight miles an hour.
claims.description: Describes a multi-speed moving-platform system on the Inner Circle line, with graduated platforms reaching 28 mph, replacing the sulphurous underground trains.

claims.quote: That fifty miles an hour, most authorities are agreed, is the limit of our speed for land travel, so far as existing conditions go.
claims.description: States that conventional rail is limited to about 50 mph without revolutionary reconstruction or a new competing mode.
